title: Morphologic learning distinguishes CLL progression patterns in biopsy tissue
summary: A random forest combined nuclear size, staining intensity, cell density and cell spacing to distinguish chronic lymphocytic leukemia, accelerated CLL and Richter transformation in biopsy regions. The combined model reported 82.4% region-level accuracy with patient-separated evaluation. Manual selection of informative regions and retrospective single-centre sampling limit its clinical interpretation; this does not establish autonomous patient diagnosis or treatment benefit.
organization: University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Patient-separated biopsy-region classification against expert-confirmed lymphoma categories, with repeated patient-level splitting.
evidence.unknown: Prospective diagnostic performance and clinical benefit remain unestablished; manually selected regions excluded difficult artifacts and residual disease patterns.
evidence.ai_role: A random forest learns diagnostic relationships among quantified cytologic and spatial tissue features.
